name: White Oak Mountain
summary: White Oak Mountain tower near Waldron: a 48-foot tower nearly complete in 1928, an 85-foot steel tower described in 1971, removed note in 1974; summit now a Forest Service electronic site.
design: 1928 item: 48-foot lookout tower; 1971 Forest Service station description: four-legged steel tower with a metal cabin, 85 feet overall
status_note: The only removal note is '1974: Removed' on a page that covers both candidate towers without naming one; no source says what became of the 85-foot tower after 1971; the summit now hosts communications sites
agency: U.S. Forest Service (per the 1971 station description); Ouachita National Forest (page heading); the station is on property the state leases

access.note: No source read describes public access to the summit; Forest Service notices list communications sites under special use authorizations

events.note: Harrison Times item of October 5, 1928, quoted on the Central lookouts page, calls a 'Waldron--48 foot lookout tower on White Oak Mt.' nearly complete
Forest Service describes the White Oak station: four-legged steel tower with metal cabin, 85 feet overall, located by distance from Clarksville, Ozark and Altus
Central lookouts page entry reads '1974: Removed'; the page does not say which tower

links.label: Ouachita National Forest project archive (USDA Forest Service)

conflicts.note: Research (2026-10-10) gives unknown where the source records give gone. The page shows the researched status; please tell us if it is wrong.
